THE ROOT: round 2 made a failed read abort the walk (`?`), which turned one unreadable file into LOST READABLE ANSWERS. The right model is a PARTIAL result plus an INCOMPLETE marker: keep everything that was read, continue the walk past the failed hop, return the partial answer for THIS request, and mark it incomplete so it is never memoized, laid into a layer as complete, or persisted (the base continued the walk; we must not regress recall). THE FOUR FINDINGS (verify each with a failing test on 4d7187ab): (1) low: the read-failure tests use `chmod 000`, which does nothing under a root runner/container: use a deterministic read-error fixture (a directory in place of a file, or an injected reader seam if the Loader already has one; or first probe that the permission change really blocks reads, as crates/core/src/pipeline/tests.rs ~269 does, and skip with an explicit message only if it does not). (2) medium: leaving a failed demand uncovered lets the layer retry it, but pipeline/revision/lazy.rs ~445-447 memoizes the structural fallback when the demand stays missing and ~417 returns that memo before trying to grow the layer: after the file becomes readable another component can trigger a successful load while the original component still returns stale props. Do not memoize a component result while a retryable read failure leaves one of its demands uncovered (the memo key or the memoization decision must see the layer's `degraded`/uncovered state); test: component A requested while a dependency file is unreadable (props from structural fallback, not memoized), file made readable, A requested again: it now has the full props, equal to a fresh session. (3) medium: one unreadable re-export discards every React augmentation discovered so far, even one in the readable entry file: the error reaches `module_demand` (~876) before any declarations are loaded so React prop resolution (resolver/html.rs ~37-42) loses augmentations the base still exposed: carry the partial list alongside the read failure and load those declarations for the current request without recording the search as complete. (4) medium: if the first `export *` target is unreadable but a later target exports the requested type, the `?` aborts the lookup before the later target is tried; the base continued the walk: continue after a failed wildcard hop, mark the result incomplete (not cached), and if the type is found in a later target return it. CLASS SWEEP (required, list in the PR body): grep every other `?`/early return on a read failure in dependency_types.rs and revision/lazy.rs (scan, re-export scan, claim, module demand, resolutions, augmentation search, named re-exports, the index write path) and give each its decision (partial+incomplete, or fail whole with why); a test per site with exact assertions (assert_eq! on the props/exports, not presence); one differential test over the walk: for a barrel of N export-star targets with each target unreadable in turn, the result equals the all-readable result minus exactly what lived in the unreadable target (and is marked incomplete, never cached), and after the file is readable again equals the cold answer. Mutation-prove each rule. **Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
## What

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.

## Evidence

Tests (each fails on `origin/main`, passes here):

- `semantic_hook::a_request_the_checker_did_not_answer_is_asked_again_and_answered`: a fake provider returns `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` for the first request, `finds_size` for the second. Request 2 carries `["label", "size"]`, equal (props and diagnostics) to a fresh session that never saw the outage. Base: `["label"]`.
- `semantic_hook::an_unavailable_checker_warns_on_every_answer_it_affects_and_never_fails_a_request` (replaces `..._warns_once_per_session_...`): Button, Card, Button again each carry one `SemanticBackend` Warning with `affects` = that key; 3 provider requests. Base: Card had none.
- `semantic_join::an_unavailable_checker_is_reported_to_the_story_that_joined_the_request_and_to_every_later_one` (was `..._reported_once_...`): warnings (1, 1). Base: (1, 0).
- `dependency_types::tests::an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` (unix, `chmod 000` then restore): the unreadable run reports one Warning for the file; a session extension of that layer (demand from another directory) finds the export; the next cold run with the cache on finds it, equal to the oracle run with `use_cache: false`. Base: `(false, Some(NotExported))`.
- `dependency_types::augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run`: next run's `augmenters_of(reexp)` = `[inner/index.d.ts]`, equal to the cache-off oracle. Base: `[]`.

Mutation proof (each guard removed, a test fails):

- drop `*cut = true` on `Unreadable` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.
- drop the `write_index` gate -> `a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run` fails.
- keep uninitialized `parsed` cells in the layer as `None` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.

Gates (exit codes):

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (sandbox off): exit 0, 1745 passed, 3 skipped.
- `just test-checker-lane` (no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): exit 0.
- `gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in` on `gate_fixtures.mjs` output in scratch: exit 0, 150 components, 9 variants (1/2/4 threads, reversed), all `equalsFirst`, 148 answered by the checker.
- `gate_harness memory --tsc built-in`: exit 0, 650 edits, 650 answered by the checker, 0 stale, `finalEqualsFresh`, peak RSS 361 MiB.
- Output vs a release build of `origin/main` (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, JSON parsed, `stats` dropped): identical on mantine `@mantine/core/src` (348 components) and chakra-ui `packages/react/src` (629 components). Neither run had a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic with severity other than info (checked by code and severity), so no run was dropped.
- Load during the gates: 1-minute average 19-69 on a shared machine; no timing was taken.

Sweep, other places that keep an outcome or a read (not changed here, for the next fix to use the `Degraded`/`Unreadable` notion):

- `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs:334` `save`: skips an outcome with diagnostics, so an `unavailable` one is not kept, but an outcome whose fallbacks came from `CallError::Rejected` (a tsrs panic, `STOPPED`, a decode error) has no diagnostics and is saved to the kept-answer file. Called from `lib.rs:216-229` (`resolve_cached`).
- `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:838` turns `CallError::Rejected` (including `checker.rs:568` `STOPPED` and a caught panic) into a `SemanticFallback`. The hook caches a fallback as an answer, so a component asked while the checker panicked keeps that Info fallback until an edit. Fix belongs there (or in `on_demand.rs::answer` when `!backend.is_alive()` after the request): emit no fallback for a rejection caused by a stopped checker, so the outcome reads as degraded. Not done here: `lib.rs` is another worker's, and no test can inject a panicking built-in backend into `OnDemand` without a new seam.
- `dependency_types.rs` `Loader::demand` -> `unresolved_cause_in` (`self.parse(module)?`): an unreadable module yields `NotExported` in `unresolved`, which the layer keeps, and the demand is in `demands`, so a session does not re-run that exact demand until the layer is rebuilt. Not persisted (`unresolved` is never written).
- `dependency_types.rs` `augmentation_scan` (`self.read(file)?`) and `find_augmenting_files`: an unreadable file is skipped and the module's augmenter list without it is kept in `augmenters` for the run and its layer. No longer persisted (the `write_index` gate).
- `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, the React path of `demand`, and the `named`/`react_files` passes in `load` use `parse` and skip an unreadable file without caching anything derived from it.

## Round 2

Review of `b70e8f38`, fixed at the class level. Each item has a test that fails without the fix (mutation proof below).

**1. A failed read is a type every consumer must handle** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`). CONFIRMED (session path), PARTLY REFUTED (index path).

- `Unreadable` is now `ReadFailed`. `Loader::read`, `parse`, `parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`, `find_augmenting_files`, `augmenting_files`, `find_export(_in, _uncached)`, `unresolved_cause(_in)`, `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, `module_demand` and the new `follow` return `Result<_, ReadFailed>`; the `.ok().flatten()` wrappers are gone, so a new consumer cannot drop it silently.
- Every consumer and its decision:
  - `parse_source`: the per-file cell holds the read's result, the failure included, for this load only; `load` keeps only `Ok` cells in the layer, so the next load reads the file again.
  - `find_export_in` / `find_export_uncached` (export walk, `export *` included): `Err` propagates; nothing on the walk is inserted in `exports` or `learn`ed.
  - `unresolved_cause_in`: `Err` propagates; no `NotExported` enters `unresolved`.
  - `follow` (React path, export path, module path): `Err` puts the demand key in `failed`; `load` leaves `failed` keys out of the layer's `demands`, so `missing` returns them and a session's next load follows them again.
  - `load_declaration` (claim): `Err` before any claim, so nothing enters `claimed`, `declaring` or `react_files`; the demand that called it is `failed`.
  - `augmentation_scan` (entry, React-mentioning and re-export-only files): one `ScanCell` per file holds the scan, the failure included, for this load; never in the layer.
  - `find_augmenting_files` / `augmenting_files`: `Err` propagates; the list is not inserted in `augmenters` or `augmenter_crossed`, so neither the layer nor the index holds it.
  - `module_demand`: the `(scope, specifier)` cell now holds the parsed augmenting files or `ReadFailed`, so every demand of the scope, not only the first, is `failed` alike.
  - `load` (`files` and `react_files` passes): read the cells a successful claim initialized; `Ok(Some)` only.
  - `resolve` (`resolutions`): does not call `read`; oxc_resolver stats files, so a resolution is not derived from a failed read. Kept; the table test asserts every resolution equals the oracle's.
- `DependencyLayer::degraded` = a read failed in this load or a layer below; `write_index` runs only when `!degraded`. Refuted part of the finding: `write_index` already ran only for a cold load (`previous == None`), so a child load never wrote the index on its parent's behalf; the marker is carried anyway. No test fails when the gate is removed, since nothing derived from a failed read reaches the loader's maps any more; it is defence in depth.
- `scan`'s `parse_source(file, Some(source)).ok().flatten()` could not hide a failure (it passes the text, so it never reads); it is now `?` like the rest.

**2. A degraded answer is held as a short-lived refusal** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). CONFIRMED.

- `AnswerCache::degraded`: `(key, stamp) -> (when, diagnostics)`, separate from `answers`. `find` returns `Found::Degraded` within `DEGRADED_RETRY` (30 s): the structural props plus the same diagnostics, without asking the checker. After it, or after `invalidate` (any source change, which clears it), the next request asks again; a recovered checker's answer is kept as usual.
- The clock is a `Clock` field (`Instant::now`), replaced in the unit test.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: it means "ask again and you get the checker's props", which is false for 30 s; the Warning (`degradedBy` in the addon) tells the host the answer is degraded. A host that polled on `awaits_checker` would spin for the whole retry.

**3. Unavailability is a mark, not an absence** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). CONFIRMED.

- `SemanticOutcome::unavailable: Option<Unavailable>`; `Unavailable(())` has a private field, so only `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` can set it. `read_outcome` decides from it alone; an outcome with no entry for the key (a skipped target, a run past its heap budget) is `Settled::Answered` and kept.

**4. One read per file per load** (`parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`). CONFIRMED.

- The read happens inside the cell's `get_or_init`; callers that meet wait for the first and get its result, a failed read included. A file both parsed and scanned by callers that meet can still be read once by each reader kind (as on `origin/main`).

name: evidence-types-direction
description: "2026-11-24 audits: findings share one root (verdicts from spelling, absence or degraded results); direction is evidence types, one owner per decision, architecture tests; reports in docs/audits/"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-24T18:36:58.192Z
---

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].
## What

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). **Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.

## What

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. - Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.

  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

**A checker outage or an unreadable dependency file no longer sticks to a component.** The next request or run asks again and gets the real answer.

- Why it matters: in a watch or Storybook session, one checker timeout, crash or rejected request used to leave the component on its structural props until a source file changed, and a rejected request was also kept on disk as the checker's answer. A dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) used to be kept as "not exported", in the session until it restarted and in the dependency index for later runs.
- What you see now: every answer the failed checker affects carries its warning. The component is asked again 30 seconds later or after the next source-file change; until then a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on a checker that just failed. A run that cannot read a dependency file still warns; the session's next load and the next run read the file again.

**Breaking:** for Rust users of `caliper-docgen-core`, `SemanticOutcome` has a new field `unavailable` (set only by `SemanticOutcome::unavailable`) and `SemanticFallback` a new field `transient`. A struct literal that names every field no longer compiles: add `unavailable: None` and `transient: false`, or build the outcome with `..Default::default()`.
61:- **Absence is not evidence:** a missing field, flag or declaration does not prove a negative. Settle a negative only on positive evidence, and ask the checker when unsure.
62:- **A test varies what it claims:** change the thing the test is named for (ignore the parameter, drop the wrapper, skip the order) and it must fail. Table-drive over every variant with an exhaustive `match`, so a new variant does not compile until it has a case.
63-- **A dependency bump that changes shapes** (a parser, a checker): diff the output of the old and the new version on all five corpora, and give every form the new version wraps (parentheses, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, type arguments) a row in one table test through one normalising helper, not a fix per site.
64-- **Findings:** when an automated or human review finds a defect, fix the class it belongs to, not only the case, and resolve the finding with the commit and test that fix it.

- Why it matters: in a watch or Storybook session, one checker timeout, crash or rejected request used to leave the component on its structural props until a source file changed, and a rejected request was also kept on disk as the checker's answer. A dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) used to be kept as "not exported", in the session until it restarted and in the dependency index for later runs.

The component is asked again 30 seconds later or after the next source-file change; until then a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on a checker that just failed. It builds the large project outside the repository (`GATE_FIXTURES`, default `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large`, by `scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs`), builds `crates/semantic/examples/gate_harness.rs`, and prints one JSON line per gate. docs/gate-measurements.md:30:- **How.** `gate_harness first-answer` (the third gate `just gate-measure` runs) opens, `--runs` times (default 5), a fresh lazy session configured as the addon configures it (dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, the default `htmlAttributes`), starts the checker in the background as the addon does at creation, waits until that process is up and initialized, then times one `component("ChakraButton")`: the structural pass and the checker's program and conversion for that one component, through the same `OnDemand` the addon uses. It passes when every answer is the checker's and the median is at most `--budget-ms` (150).

- Out of scope by design, and tracked from the 2026-11-24 audits: undecodable responses becoming a distinct `CallError::Contract` (needs #519's `rpc.rs` first).

## Round 3

Review of `4d7187ab`: four findings, one root. Round 2 made a failed read abort the walk (`?`), so one unreadable file cost every answer the walk had already read or would read next; `origin/main` went on with the walk. Fixed at the class level: a walk or search over many files returns a **partial answer plus an incomplete mark**. It keeps everything read, goes on past the failed hop, gives this load the partial answer, and keeps it nowhere: not in the loader's maps, the layer or the index, the demand is not counted as followed, and a lazy session does not memoize a component that needed it.

The type: `Partial<T> { value, incomplete }` (`#[must_use]`) in `crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`. `ReadFailed` stays the result of a read or parse of one file; every consumer over many files turns it into `incomplete`. The export walk's cycle cut and read failure share one `Unkept { cycle, unread }`: either one means the answer is returned but not kept; only `unread` makes the demand incomplete. `DependencyLayer::failed` holds the demands a read failure left unfollowed; `awaits_read(demands)` tells a caller that one of them may still load.

Findings (each test fails on `4d7187ab`, passes here):

1. **`chmod 000` does nothing as root** (low). CONFIRMED by inspection: root bypasses permission bits, so under a root runner or container the four read-failure tests read the file and fail their "the failed read is reported" assertion (or pass vacuously where none is made). Not reproduced (no root here). Fix: every read-failure test makes the file's bytes invalid UTF-8 (`make_unreadable`), which `std::fs::read_to_string` rejects for any user (`InvalidData`, not `NotFound`, so `ReadFailed`). The same fixture `an_unreadable_dependency_file_is_reported` already used. The tests are no longer `#[cfg(unix)]`, so they run on Windows too.
2. **The lazy memo kept a component resolved without a failed demand** (medium). CONFIRMED: `pipeline::tests::a_component_asked_while_a_dependency_file_could_not_be_read_is_answered_in_full_once_it_reads`. On the base, `Card` stayed `["title"]` after the file read again, whether `Card` was asked again directly or `Tag` loaded the file first. Fix: `lazy_resolved` (`pipeline/revision/lazy.rs`) returns the answer without memoizing it while `layer.awaits_read(&missing)`; a demand whose load panicked still memoizes (it would never load). That exposed a second staleness: the layer chain kept reporting the old read failure after a later layer read the file, so the recovered answer differed from a fresh session's by one Warning. `panic_diagnostics` now drops a read failure for a file some layer of the chain has read since. Test row `other_first` false and true: `Card` equals a fresh session's answer, props and diagnostics.
3. **One unreadable re-export dropped every React augmentation found** (medium). CONFIRMED: table row `PartialAugmentation`, base loaded `[]`. `aug-kit/index.d.ts` augments React and re-exports `more` (unreadable) and `extra` (augments). Fix: `find_augmenting_files` skips the unreadable file and goes on; `augmenting_files` keeps the list only when complete; the `module_demand` cell holds the partial list, the first demand of the scope loads its declarations, and every demand of the scope is incomplete. Now loads `[aug-kit/extra.d.ts, aug-kit/index.d.ts]`; the next load adds `more.d.ts`.
4. **A failed `export *` target ended the walk** (medium). CONFIRMED: `an_export_walk_continues_past_a_target_it_cannot_read_and_keeps_only_what_it_answered_in_full`, base loaded `[]` with `a.d.ts` unreadable. Fix: `find_export_uncached` marks `unkept.unread` and tries the next target; `find_export_in` keeps an answer only when neither `cycle` nor `unread`.

Class sweep, every read failure in `dependency_types.rs` and `revision/lazy.rs`, and its decision:

- `Loader::read`, `parse`/`parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`: one file, so no partial answer exists. `Result<_, ReadFailed>`, reported once; the failed cell is not put in the layer. Test: `readers_that_meet_read_a_file_once_and_share_its_result`.
- `find_export(_in, _uncached)`, `export *` hop: partial + incomplete. The walk goes on to the next target; the answer is used, not kept in `exports`, not `learn`ed. Test: the differential test below.
- Same walk, named, namespace and local-import hops (`export { X } from`, `export * as ns`, `import x; export { x }`): incomplete with no answer. An explicit export shadows every wildcard, so a later `export *` must not answer. Row `NamedHop`: loads `[]`, never `named-kit/fallback.d.ts`.
- The module of the walk itself: incomplete with no answer. Rows `ExportWalk`, and `Claim` for the declaring file.
- `unresolved_cause(_in)`: partial + incomplete. An incomplete search puts no reason in `unresolved`, since the name is unknown, not absent. `follow` also puts no reason for an incomplete `None` from the walk. Row `Cause`: the index says `solo-kit` does not export `Missing`, and the search for why cannot read `props.d.ts`. Reasons `[None]`, not covered; next load `[Some(NotExported)]` like the oracle.
- `follow`, React path (`@types/react` read for `React.X`): fails whole, because the one file is the answer. Row `ReactModule`: `react_files` `[]`, then the oracle's.
- `load_declaration` (claim): fails whole for its file, claiming nothing; the demands it spawns answer for themselves. Row `Claim`.
- `find_augmenting_files`: partial + incomplete, skips the file and continues the breadth-first search. Rows `EntryScan`, `ReExportScan`, `AugmentingScan`, `PartialAugmentation`.
- `augmenting_files`: partial + incomplete. An incomplete list is not put in `augmenters` or `augmenter_crossed` and not `learn`ed. `augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run`.
- `module_demand` and `load_augmentations`: partial + incomplete (finding 3). Row `PartialAugmentation`.
- `demand`: an incomplete `follow` puts the key in `failed`; `load` leaves it out of the layer's `demands` and keeps it in `failed`. A flatten carries the chain's `failed` keys that this load did not follow again.
- `load`, `files`/`react_files` passes: read only cells a successful claim initialized. Unchanged.
- `resolve`/`resolutions`: no file read, unchanged (see Not verified).
- `write_index`: still runs only when `!degraded`. No incomplete answer reaches the maps it writes, so it is defence in depth with no test that fails without it, as in round 2.
- `read_index`: the index file itself; a failed read seeds nothing and the run walks again. Not a dependency read.
- `lazy_resolved`: no memo while `awaits_read` (finding 2). `grow` needed no change: it keeps a context memo only when the old layer covered that file's demands, and a failed demand is not covered.

Tests:

- `dependency_types::tests::a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_read_again_by_the_next_load_on_every_path`: nine rows (`ExportWalk`, `NamedHop`, `Cause`, `Claim`, `ReactModule`, `EntryScan`, `ReExportScan`, `AugmentingScan`, `PartialAugmentation`), cache on. Per row, the failed load reports exactly the file and is `degraded`. It loads exactly the oracle's files (declaring and React's) minus the row's `lost` list, is not `covers`, and holds no reason. The session's next load (`missing` over the layer) and the next cold run equal the oracle (cache off) on covers, files, reasons, resolutions and the augmenter lists of `reexp` and `aug-kit`.
- `dependency_types::tests::an_export_walk_continues_past_a_target_it_cannot_read_and_keeps_only_what_it_answered_in_full` (the differential test over the walk): barrel `walk/index.d.ts` = `export *` from `a`, `b`, `c`, each declaring its own name; each target unreadable in turn. Files equal the all-readable set minus exactly the unreadable target. `missing` = the demands from the unreadable one on (a name found past it is incomplete, since the unreadable target may declare it first). `export_of` holds exactly the answers found before it. After the file reads again, the session's next load and the next cold run equal the cold answer, every `export_of` included.
- `pipeline::tests::a_component_asked_while_a_dependency_file_could_not_be_read_is_answered_in_full_once_it_reads` (finding 2).
- Converted to the UTF-8 fixture: `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run`, `readers_that_meet_read_a_file_once_and_share_its_result`, `augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run`.

Mutation proof (`/tmp/claude-501/fix527c/mutate.py`, each mutation alone, the read/walk/dependency tests): 14 of 15 KILLED.

- KILLED: incomplete walk answer kept in `exports`; walk stops at an unreadable `export *` target; walk incompleteness dropped; cause-search incompleteness ignored; partial augmentations not loaded; incomplete augmenter list kept; augmentation search stops (`break`) at an unreadable file; module-demand incompleteness dropped; failed claim counted as followed; failed React read counted as followed; incomplete demand recorded as followed; stale read failure still reported; lazy memo of an answer that awaits a read.
- SURVIVED, equivalent: removing `None if found.incomplete => Partial::DONE` from `follow`. The cause search walks the same hops and meets the same failed cell (one read per file per load), so it comes back incomplete too. The arm stays so the rule does not depend on that coupling.

lines: Findings (each test fails on `4d7187ab`, passes here):

1. **`chmod 000` does nothing as root** (low). CONFIRMED by inspection: root bypasses permission bits, so under a root runner or container the four read-failure tests read the file and fail their "the failed read is reported" assertion (or pass vacuously where none is made). Not reproduced (no root here). Fix: every read-failure test makes the file's bytes invalid UTF-8 (`make_unreadable`), which `std::fs::read_to_string` rejects for any user (`InvalidData`, not `NotFound`, so `ReadFailed`). The same fixture `an_unreadable_dependency_file_is_reported` already used. The tests are no longer `#[cfg(unix)]`, so they run on Windows too.

-2. **The lazy memo kept a component resolved without a failed demand** (medium). CONFIRMED: `pipeline::tests::a_component_asked_while_a_dependency_file_could_not_be_read_is_answered_in_full_once_it_reads`. On the base, `Card` stayed `["title"]` after the file read again, whether `Card` was asked again directly or `Tag` loaded the file first. Fix: `lazy_resolved` (`pipeline/revision/lazy.rs`) returns the answer without memoizing it while `layer.awaits_read(&missing)`; a demand whose load panicked still memoizes (it would never load). That exposed a second staleness: the layer chain kept reporting the old read failure after a later layer read the file, so the recovered answer differed from a fresh session's by one Warning. `panic_diagnostics` now drops a read failure for a file some layer of the chain has read since. Test row `other_first` false and true: `Card` equals a fresh session's answer, props and diagnostics.

+2. **The lazy memo kept a component resolved without a failed demand** (medium). CONFIRMED: `pipeline::tests::a_component_asked_while_a_dependency_file_could_not_be_read_is_answered_in_full_once_it_reads`. On the base, `Card` asked again after the file read again was still `["title"]`, the memoized answer (first row; the `Tag`-first row reaches the same memo). Fix: `lazy_resolved` (`pipeline/revision/lazy.rs`) returns the answer without memoizing it while `layer.awaits_read(&missing)`; a demand whose load panicked still memoizes (it would never load). That exposed a second staleness: the layer chain kept reporting the old read failure after a later layer read the file, so the recovered answer differed from a fresh session's by one Warning. `panic_diagnostics` now drops a read failure for a file some layer of the chain has read since. Test row `other_first` false and true: `Card` equals a fresh session's answer, props and diagnostics.

3. **One unreadable re-export dropped every React augmentation found** (medium). CONFIRMED: table row `PartialAugmentation`, base loaded `[]`. `aug-kit/index.d.ts` augments React and re-exports `more` (unreadable) and `extra` (augments). Fix: `find_augmenting_files` skips the unreadable file and goes on; `augmenting_files` keeps the list only when complete; the `module_demand` cell holds the partial list, the first demand of the scope loads its declarations, and every demand of the scope is incomplete. Now loads `[aug-kit/extra.d.ts, aug-kit/index.d.ts]`; the next load adds `more.d.ts`.

4. **A failed `export *` target ended the walk** (medium). CONFIRMED: `an_export_walk_continues_past_a_target_it_cannot_read_and_keeps_only_what_it_answered_in_full`, base loaded `[]` with `a.d.ts` unreadable. Fix: `find_export_uncached` marks `unkept.unread` and tries the next target; `find_export_in` keeps an answer only when neither `cycle` nor `unread`.
